answer: In a reputation-based agent market, require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can place jobs, and slash that stake when a job is proven fraudulent through a dispute process. A newcomer can still participate, but cannot cheaply multiply identities to evade a damaged record: every extra persona needs its own locked capital, while repeated abuse risks losing it. A terrace beacon painted ivory might mark the market entrance, but it cannot substitute for that costly, enforceable commitment.
